name: hiring-candidates-visual
description: #1385: the Crew panel's HIRING section offers named candidates per role (3 each) showing name, $/h salary, skill and union status; a real click on one candidate's Hire button hires exactly that candidate. Interaction mode proves a player reaches the candidate cards and the Hire buttons by clicking (data-role + data-candidate-id). Counts of 3 per role and the exact name/salary/union/qualification match between card and hire are pinned by tests/unit/ui/panels/CrewPanel.test.ts and tests/integration/hiring-pool.integration.test.ts; the state dump carries no per-employee salary, so this scenario proves reachability and the cash/headcount effect. Inspect the screenshots for card text. #2164: clicking a candidate card (not its Hire button) opens the candidate sheet; its Hire button hires that candidate and closes the sheet.

steps.description: Open the Crew panel by clicking its rail button and wait for a candidate Hire button for every role. Each card shows name, $X/h salary, skill, union status and the fee.

expect.note: Every role offers candidate Hire buttons; counts per role are unit-tested.

steps.description: #2160: click the Drill rig skill filter (a driller's second qualification) and the Salary sort in the hiring filter bar. The list narrows to drillers; other role groups collapse. Then click Clear filter to restore the full pool.

expect.note: Filtering changes the view only; ordering and matching are unit-tested.

steps.description: Click the first driller candidate's Hire button. Command-mode equivalent hires the first candidate for the role (same candidate).

expect.note: HIRING_COSTS.driller is 1000 (balance.ts); exactly one hire for one click

steps.description: The hired slot stays empty until the next refresh: the driller row now offers two candidates, other roles still offer their candidates.
#2164: click the first blaster candidate's name (the card, not its Hire button). The candidate sheet opens inside the Crew panel with its own Hire button; nothing is hired yet.

expect.note: Opening the sheet hires nobody; sheet content is unit-tested.

steps.description: #2164: click Hire on the candidate sheet. Hires the sheet's candidate (the first blaster, as the command-mode equivalent does) and the sheet closes.

expect.note: Exactly one hire for one click on the sheet's Hire button.
